# Testing the new pricing/billing implementation

This documents how to set up, test, and validate the plan-tier billing system
implemented per `pricing_research.md`: Free / Normal / Pro plans, account-wide
voice quotas, a 30-second voice recording cap, mortgage interest vs. principal
categories, tax-ready export gating, and (section 7 below) native iOS/Android
billing via RevenueCat.

## 1. Run the new database migrations (required — no auto-migration exists)

`Base.metadata.create_all()` only creates *missing tables*, it never alters
existing ones. Since `organization_billing` and `financial_records` already
exist in your database, you must run these SQL files by hand against your
Postgres DB before starting the backend:

```pwsh
psql -U postgres -d rentzu -f schema_updates\2026-07-18-organization-billing-plan-tiers.sql
psql -U postgres -d rentzu -f schema_updates\2026-07-18-financial-record-add-mortgage-category.sql
psql -U postgres -d rentzu -f schema_updates\2026-07-25-organization-billing-add-revenuecat.sql
```

(Adjust `-U`/`-d` to match your `DATABASE_URL`.) All are idempotent
(`add column if not exists`, `drop constraint if exists` before re-adding), so
re-running them is safe.

## 2. Set up Stripe (test mode)

You do **not** need real payment info — use Stripe's test mode throughout.

1. Create a free Stripe account (or use an existing one) and switch to **Test mode** (toggle top-right in the Stripe Dashboard).
2. Get your test API keys: Developers → API keys.
   - `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` = the "Secret key" (starts `sk_test_...`)
   - `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` = the "Publishable key" (starts `pk_test_...`) — not currently used by the app UI, but keep it set for future Stripe Elements work.
3. Create 4 recurring Products/Prices (Products → Add product). Each plan needs
   a monthly and a yearly **per-unit** price (Stripe will multiply price × the
   `quantity` we send at checkout, which is the account's total unit count):

   | Product      | Price                | Billing period | Suggested amount |
   |--------------|-----------------------|-----------------|-------------------|
   | Rentzu Normal | STRIPE_PRICE_NORMAL_MONTHLY | Monthly | $1.99 |
   | Rentzu Normal | STRIPE_PRICE_NORMAL_YEARLY  | Yearly  | $19.99 |
   | Rentzu Pro    | STRIPE_PRICE_PRO_MONTHLY    | Monthly | $2.99 |
   | Rentzu Pro    | STRIPE_PRICE_PRO_YEARLY     | Yearly  | $29.00 |

   Copy each Price's ID (starts `price_...`) into the matching env var below.
4. Set up the webhook (Developers → Webhooks → Add endpoint), or for local
   testing use the Stripe CLI instead (easier — no public URL needed):
   ```pwsh
   stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8000/billing/webhook
   ```
   This prints a `whsec_...` value — that's your `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

## 3. Fill in your `.env`

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` if you haven't already, then set (see the
"Plan-tier billing" section added to `.env.example` for the full list):

```
STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_...
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_...
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_...
STRIPE_PRICE_NORMAL_MONTHLY=price_...
STRIPE_PRICE_NORMAL_YEARLY=price_...
STRIPE_PRICE_PRO_MONTHLY=price_...
STRIPE_PRICE_PRO_YEARLY=price_...
```

The `RENTZU_PRICE_*_CENTS`, `RENTZU_*_VOICE_QUOTA*`, and
`RENTZU_MAX_VOICE_SECONDS` vars already have sensible defaults matching
`pricing_research.md` — you only need to override them if you want to test
different numbers.

## 4. Start the backend and (if testing webhooks locally) the Stripe CLI listener

```pwsh
cd server\src
python -m uvicorn main:app --reload
```

In a second terminal, if testing checkout end-to-end:
```pwsh
stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8000/billing/webhook
```

## 5. What to expect — manual test scenarios

### A. Free plan (default, no Stripe interaction needed)
- New organizations start on `plan: "free"`.
- `GET /billing/overview?organization_id=...` should return `plan: "free"`,
  `exports_allowed: false`, `voice_quota.limit: 3`.
- Create as many properties/units as you want — free accounts are **not**
  blocked from adding units (per the "give away units, meter voice/exports"
  strategy).
- Use voice-to-text 3 times in a rolling 30-day window → the 4th attempt on
  `/voice/transcribe` should return **HTTP 402** with a message like
  `"Voice quota exceeded (3/3 used this period)..."`.
- Try downloading a Schedule E or Property Expense PDF from the Tax Ready tab
  → expect an **"Upgrade required"** alert (backend returns 402).

### B. Voice recording length cap
- Record a voice note longer than 30 seconds. The app should auto-stop and
  submit at exactly 30s (client-side timer in `useVoiceRecorder.ts`).
- To test the server-side cap independently, upload an audio file longer than
  ~31s directly to `POST /voice/transcribe` (e.g. via the `/docs` Swagger UI)
  → expect **HTTP 400** `"Voice recording is too long..."`.
  - Note: if `ffprobe` isn't installed, the server falls back to a size-based
    duration estimate (assumes ~64kbps encoding); install ffmpeg/ffprobe
    (already referenced in `services/audio_convert.py`) for exact duration.

### C. Upgrading to Normal or Pro (Stripe test checkout)
1. In the app, go to Account tab → Plan card. On a free-plan org you'll see
   plan buttons (Normal / Pro) and interval buttons (Monthly / Yearly).
2. Pick a plan+interval and tap the "Upgrade to ..." button — this opens a
   Stripe Checkout page in the browser.
3. Use Stripe's test card `4242 4242 4242 4242`, any future expiry date, any
   CVC, any ZIP.
4. After payment, Stripe redirects to `STRIPE_CHECKOUT_SUCCESS_URL` (a
   placeholder `example.com` URL by default — fine for testing, just close the
   browser tab and return to the app).
5. Within a few seconds (once the webhook is processed — instant if using
   `stripe listen`), `GET /billing/overview` should now show your chosen
   `plan`/`billing_interval`, `exports_allowed: true`, and a higher
   `voice_quota.limit` (10 × total units for Normal, 30 × total units for Pro).
6. Tax Ready PDF downloads should now succeed instead of showing the upgrade
   alert.

### D. Adding/removing units on a paid account
- With an active paid subscription, add another property/unit, then call
  `POST /billing/sync-subscription-units` (or trigger it from wherever the app
  calls it) — the Stripe subscription quantity should update to match your new
  total unit count, and Stripe will show a prorated invoice. Voice quota should
  scale accordingly (10 or 30 more per unit).

### E. Canceling / downgrading
- Use "Manage billing" (Stripe Customer Portal) to cancel the subscription.
- Once Stripe fires `customer.subscription.deleted` (or a similar terminal
  status), the webhook sets the org back to `plan: "free"`, exports become
  gated again, and voice quota drops back to 3/month flat.

### F. Mortgage category (separate from billing, same session's work)
- Add an expense record with category "Mortgage Interest" → should appear as
  its own line ("Mortgage Interest") on the Schedule E PDF and count toward
  deductible expenses.
- Add an expense record with category "Mortgage Principal (non-deductible)" →
  should show in the transaction list but **not** reduce the deductible
  expense total or appear as a deduction on Schedule E.

## 7. Native mobile billing (RevenueCat) — setup and testing

This is the iOS/Android in-app-purchase path added 07/25/2026 (see
`pricing_research.md`'s "Native mobile billing (RevenueCat)" section). It
requires several external accounts/dashboards before it can be tested — none
of this can be simulated without them.

### 7a. Prerequisites (external setup, not in this repo)
1. **Apple Developer Program** ($99/yr) and/or **Google Play Console**
   ($25 one-time) enrollment.
2. Create **subscription products** for Normal + Pro, monthly + yearly (4
   products) in **App Store Connect**, and the equivalent 4 in **Google Play
   Console**.
3. Create a free **RevenueCat** account/project (revenuecat.com), add your
   iOS/Android apps, and:
   - Attach the store products to **two Entitlements** — pick identifiers,
     e.g. `normal_access` and `pro_access`.
   - Copy the **public API keys** (Project Settings → API Keys) for iOS and
     Android.
   - Set up a **Webhook** (Project Settings → Integrations → Webhooks) with
     your backend's `POST /billing/revenuecat/webhook` URL, and set an
     **Authorization header value** — this is your shared secret.

### 7a-bis. Current configured state (as of 08/01/2026)
The RevenueCat project ("Rentzu", id `97a79870`) is configured against a
**Test Store** app, which simulates purchases without needing App Store /
Play Store products to exist yet. This is what the app currently talks to.

| RevenueCat object | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Entitlements | `normal_access`, `pro_access` |
| Products (Test Store) | `normal_monthly` $1.99, `normal_yearly` $19.99, `pro_monthly` $2.99, `pro_yearly` $29.00 |
| Offering `default` ("Rentzu Normal") | `$rc_monthly` → `normal_monthly`, `$rc_annual` → `normal_yearly` |
| Offering `pro` ("Rentzu Pro") | `$rc_monthly` → `pro_monthly`, `$rc_annual` → `pro_yearly` |

**One Offering per paid plan** is the structure the app now depends on:
`getOfferingPackagesForPlan(plan)` in `app/src/services/revenueCat.ts` looks up
the offering whose identifier matches the plan name, then picks the package by
interval. Normal maps to the pre-created `default` offering because RevenueCat
offering identifiers are immutable, so `revenueCat.ts` keeps an explicit
`normal → default` fallback — rename or recreate that offering as `normal` and
the fallback stops being needed.

Still outstanding for real (non-test) billing:
- Google Play Console subscription products for `com.rocmaxrealty.rentzu`
  (Play requires an uploaded APK/AAB before subscriptions can be created).
- A Google Play service account + Play Developer API key connected to
  RevenueCat as a "Google Play" app, with the real products attached to the
  same two entitlements.
- The webhook (needs a publicly reachable backend URL; `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTHORIZATION`
  is already generated in the server `.env`).
- Expo SDK 51 / RN 0.74 native libs are **not 16 KB page aligned**, which
  Google Play now requires for new/updated apps — an SDK upgrade is needed
  before a Play Store release (it is only a warning during local testing).

### 7b. Configure env vars
Server `.env` (see the "Native mobile billing (RevenueCat)" section added to
`.env.example`):
```
REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_NORMAL=normal_access
REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_PRO=pro_access
REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTHORIZATION=<same secret as RevenueCat's webhook config>
```
Verify with `GET /billing/plans` — each paid plan must report its
`revenuecat_entitlement_id`, otherwise the app falls back to the Stripe flow.

App `app/.env` (copy from `app/.env.example`):
```
EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_IOS_SDK_KEY=<from RevenueCat dashboard>
EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_ANDROID_SDK_KEY=<from RevenueCat dashboard>
```
The Test Store's key (prefix `test_`) works for both platforms. These are
inlined at bundle time, so restart Metro with `--clear` after changing them.

### 7c. Build a dev client (Expo Go will NOT work)
`react-native-purchases` is a native module — it isn't available in Expo Go.
```pwsh
cd app
npx eas build --profile development --platform ios     # or android
```
Install the resulting dev client build on a real device or simulator/emulator
(native IAP generally does not work on iOS Simulator — use a real device or
Android emulator with Play Store signed in), then run `npx expo start --dev-client`.

### 7d. Manual test scenarios
- **Purchase (Free → paid):** Account tab → Plan card → pick Normal/Pro +
  interval → tap "Upgrade to ...". This calls `ensureRevenueCatConfigured`
  (sets RevenueCat's `appUserID` to the organization id), fetches the current
  offering, purchases the matching package, then calls
  `POST /billing/revenuecat/sync` — `GET /billing/overview` should now show
  `billing_provider: "revenuecat"`, the new `plan`, and a scaled voice quota.
  Use each store's sandbox/test-track purchase flow (App Store Connect
  Sandbox tester account / Play Console license tester) — do not use real money.
- **Restore purchases:** on a free-looking org that actually has an active
  store subscription (e.g. reinstalled app), tap "Restore purchases" — should
  call `restoreRevenueCatPurchases` then sync and pick up the existing plan.
- **Manage/cancel:** on a paid RevenueCat-billed org, the button becomes
  "Manage subscription" and deep-links to the OS's native subscription
  settings (`itms-apps://apps.apple.com/account/subscriptions` on iOS,
  Play Store's subscriptions page on Android) — cancel there.
- **Webhook-driven downgrade:** after cancelling in the store sandbox, wait
  for RevenueCat to fire an `EXPIRATION` event (or use RevenueCat's dashboard
  "Send test webhook" tool) → `POST /billing/revenuecat/webhook` should flip
  the org back to `plan: "free"`. Verify `revenuecat_events` has a row and
  that resending the same event id is a no-op (de-dupe).
- **Cross-provider guard:** on an org already `billing_provider: "revenuecat"`
  and paid, confirm `POST /billing/checkout-session` (Stripe, web) now
  returns **HTTP 400** instead of creating a duplicate subscription.

## 8. Known limitations / things you may still want to do

- `STRIPE_CHECKOUT_SUCCESS_URL` / `CANCEL_URL` / `CUSTOMER_PORTAL_RETURN_URL`
  default to `https://example.com/...` placeholders — fine for manual testing,
  but replace with a real deep link or hosted page before shipping so the
  in-app flow can detect "checkout complete" without the user manually
  switching back to the app.
- The Plan card UI is intentionally minimal (plan/interval chip selectors) to
  match the "fast rollout" priority — polish later if desired.
- RevenueCat's package-to-plan matching in `App.tsx` (`purchaseSelectedPlanNative`)
  guesses the right package by checking if its identifier contains the plan
  name or "annual"/"monthly" — this depends on how you name packages in the
  RevenueCat dashboard; adjust the matching logic or (better) name your
  packages consistently (e.g. `$rc_monthly`/`$rc_annual` with one Offering
  per plan) once real products exist.
- No automated tests exist for this flow (repo has no test suite); all
  validation above is manual, consistent with the rest of this repo.
